assessments.reasoning: Borland's 2002 Object Pascal guide, chapter 2, Program organization, says programs are usually divided into source-code units and the program heading precedes an optional uses clause.

challenge.method: Checked the guide's title and copyright pages and read the audience and organization paragraphs on printed page 2-1 for edition scope and signs of mandatory modularization.
challenge.results: The manual explicitly qualifies typical modularization and makes uses optional. Delphi and Kylix appear as Borland development tool examples.

limitations: This is the organization described for the Borland variety in the cited guide. Other Object Pascal traditions require their own sources.
